verses.zh: （ 可 拉 後 裔 的 詩 歌 。 ） 耶 和 華 所 立 的 根 基 在 聖 山 上 。
verses.en: Written by the Korahites; a psalm, a song.The Lord’s city is in the holy hills.
notes: Psalm 87. The psalmist celebrates the Lord’s presence in Zion and the special status of its citizens.

verses.zh: 他 愛 錫 安 的 門 ， 勝 於 愛 雅 各 一 切 的 住 處 。
verses.en: The Lord loves the gates of Zionmore than all the dwelling places of Jacob.

verses.zh: 神 的 城 啊 ， 有 榮 耀 的 事 乃 指 著 你 說 的 。 （ 細 拉 ）
verses.en: People say wonderful things about you, O city of God. (Selah)
notes: Psalm 87. The psalmist celebrates the Lord’s presence in Zion and the special status of its citizens.

verses.zh: 我 要 提 起 拉 哈 伯 和 巴 比 倫 人 ， 是 在 認 識 我 之 中 的 ； 看 哪 ， 非 利 士 和 推 羅 並 古 實 人 ， 個 個 生 在 那 裡 。
verses.en: I mention Rahab and Babylon to my followers. Here are Philistia and Tyre, along with Ethiopia. It is said of them, “This one was born there.”
notes: Psalm 87. The psalmist celebrates the Lord’s presence in Zion and the special status of its citizens.

Heb “his foundation [is] in the hills of holiness.” The expression “his foundation” refers here by metonymy to the Lord’s dwelling place in Zion. The “hills” are the ones surrounding Zion (see Pss 125:2; 133:3).

Heb “glorious things are spoken about you.” The translation assumes this is a general reference to compliments paid to Zion by those who live within her walls and by those who live in the surrounding areas and lands. Another option is that this refers to a prophetic oracle about the city’s glorious future. In this case one could translate, “wonderful things are announced concerning you.”
“Rahab,” which means “proud one,” is used here as a title for Egypt (see Isa 30:7).

Heb “to those who know me” (see Ps 36:10). Apparently the Lord speaks here. The verbal construction (the Hiphil of זָכַר, zakhar, “remember” followed by the preposition ל [lamed] with a substantive) is rare, but the prepositional phrase is best understood as indicating the recipient of the announcement (see Jer 4:16). Some take the preposition in the sense of “among” and translate, “among those who know me” (cf. NEB, NIV, NRSV). In this case these foreigners are viewed as the Lord’s people and the psalm is interpreted as anticipating a time when all nations will worship the Lord (see Ps 86:9) and be considered citizens of Zion.

verses.zh: 論 到 錫 安 ， 必 說 ： 這 一 個 、 那 一 個 都 生 在 其 中 ， 而 且 至 高 者 必 親 自 堅 立 這 城 。
verses.en: But it is said of Zion’s residents, “Each one of these was born in her,and the Most High makes her secure.”
notes: Psalm 87. The psalmist celebrates the Lord’s presence in Zion and the special status of its citizens.

verses.zh: 當 耶 和 華 記 錄 萬 民 的 時 候 ， 他 要 點 出 這 一 個 生 在 那 裡 。 （ 細 拉 ）
verses.en: The Lord writes in the census book of the nations, “This one was born there.” (Selah)
notes: Psalm 87. The psalmist celebrates the Lord’s presence in Zion and the special status of its citizens.

verses.zh: 歌 唱 的 ， 跳 舞 的 ， 都 要 說 ： 我 的 泉 源 都 在 你 裡 面 。
verses.en: As for the singers, as well as the pipers—all of them sing within your walls.
notes: Psalm 87. The psalmist celebrates the Lord’s presence in Zion and the special status of its citizens.
